title: Cartridge artifact contracts
description: The compiled cartridge, its artifact file and the compiler and loader diagnostics (05 §8, §11, §12, §20; 08 §6; 14 §R4). R4 minimal: the frozen kinds only; rooms, NPCs, schedules, quests, dialogue, assets and localization join with their features, under a new format tag.

CompiledCartridge.description: The semantic payload a cartridge hash covers (05 §11 'Hash domains and attestations'): the manifest with its compatibility requirements, the exact capability lock (exactly requires.capabilities until a registry dependency exists; the loader rejects a difference with LOCK_MANIFEST_MISMATCH), and the normalized definitions of the frozen kinds, each map keyed by DefinitionRefString so canonical key order orders it. A key's cartridge_id and cartridge_version are the manifest's id and version and its last segment is the definition's key; the compiler guarantees this and the loader rejects a mismatch (ARTIFACT_DEFINITION_KEY_MISMATCH); the subset cannot express it. format is the hash domain tag and selects the variant; any change to a variant's shape takes a new tag, so a later field (assets, per-locale catalogs, NPCs) is a new format, never a changed hash of an existing one. No certificate, signature, package or catalog field belongs here (CAR-10). In R4 the authored cartridge.json is exactly the CartridgeManifest object form (kernel_api as {at_least, below}, capabilities as key to version); the string forms (">=1.3 <2.0", key@version) are not accepted yet.

facts.description: The cartridge's fact declarations, keyed by DefinitionRefString of kind fact.

oneOf.description: loka-cartridge-v2 (R5 slice 1): v1 plus rooms, the entry room and the default-locale text catalog. The compiler emits v2 exactly when the source has rooms, an entry or a text catalog, so a cartridge without rooms keeps its v1 bytes and hash.

CartridgeArtifact.description: The compiled artifact file: one canonical JSON document, built and never committed (05 §20). content_hash is the cartridge hash (CartridgeRelease.cartridge_hash): SHA-256 of the canonical bytes (loka-numeric-v1) of cartridge. It hashes cartridge only, never itself, so it can sit beside it (CAR-10); the loader recomputes it and rejects a mismatch.

ArtifactSize.description: The byte length of a cartridge artifact file, checked before decoding: at most 4 MiB (owner decision, docs/decisions/owner-decisions-r4-2026-09-25.md, item 2). bin/contracts.exs emits the maximum into kernel/ts/src/contracts.gen.ts as ARTIFACT_MAX_BYTES; Elixir reads it here.

DiagnosticCode.description: A diagnostic code: a closed set, one code per distinct cause (08 §6: repair loops read codes and data, never prose). INVALID_JSON: a source file is not JSON (RFC 8259, UTF-8); in the loader, the artifact is not UTF-8 or fails the canonical decoder (loka-numeric-v1), duplicate keys included, path empty, data {}; DUPLICATE_KEY: an object in a source file repeats a key (Elixir's JSON keeps the first silently, so the compiler checks it); UNKNOWN_FIELD: a field outside the registered schema (05 §5); the validator's unknown_property; in the loader, path the validator's, data {}; SCHEMA_VIOLATION: any other schema error; data.error is its ErrorCode (error_registry.json); a v2 source (rooms, an entry or text.json) without an entry is missing_property at cartridge.entry; in the loader, path the validator's; MISSING_MANIFEST: the cartridge has no cartridge.json (05 §3); path is cartridge; DUPLICATE_DEFINITION: two definitions in one cartridge have one DefinitionRef (03 §2, 05 §4; other cartridges' refs differ, CAR-01); FACT_NAME_COLLISION: two authored fact names map to one key after each . becomes _ (owner decision, IMPORT.md); FACT_DEFAULT_INVALID: a fact default is outside its enum values or int bounds (fact.schema.json FactType); UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE: a reference names no definition (CAR-02, A10); an exit's to or the entry names no room of this cartridge (05 §17), or a room's title or description has no text catalog entry, data {target} (the DefinitionRefString or the TextKey), path the reference (rooms/ferry_landing.exits.north.to, cartridge.entry, rooms/ferry_landing.title; in the loader .cartridge.rooms["..."].exits.north.to, .cartridge.entry); UNKNOWN_COMMAND: an action's command is not in the command registry (action.schema.json ActionDefinition); in the loader, no capability owns it (capability_registry.json), path .cartridge.actions["..."].command, data {}; FACT_TYPE_MISMATCH: a fact_compare value is not of the fact's type (06 §21: typed policy AST); UNKNOWN_CAPABILITY: a key in requires.capabilities is not registered at that version (A10, Gate R4); SERVER_ONLY_CAPABILITY: an offline_private cartridge requires a server_only capability (05 §6, C4); KERNEL_API_RANGE_INVALID: the kernel_api range is empty or reversed, at_least not below below (05 §3; a malformed version string is SCHEMA_VIOLATION); PINNED_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED: content_schema or rule_ir is a version the compiler or installed kernel does not implement (05 §3; both implement 1 now), data {field, declared, supported}; in the loader, path .cartridge.manifest.requires.<field>; UNDECLARED_CAPABILITY: a definition uses a command, event or policy op, or is of a definition kind (room), whose owning capability (capability_registry.json) the manifest does not require (05 §6), path the room file for a room (.cartridge.rooms["..."] in the loader), data {capability} (the owner's key), suggested_capabilities [its key@version]; in the loader, the lock lacks the owner's key, path the command or op member (.cartridge.actions["..."].command, ...policy.root.items[0].op); NESTING_TOO_DEEP: the compiled artifact would nest a definition deeper than the canonical depth limit (loka-numeric-v1), data {maximum}; the author's file is valid JSON, so this is not INVALID_JSON, while the loader reports a too-deep artifact as INVALID_JSON; ARTIFACT_TOO_LARGE: the artifact file exceeds ArtifactSize, checked before decoding, path empty, data {bytes, maximum}; UNKNOWN_FORMAT: the artifact's cartridge.format is absent or neither loka-cartridge-v1 nor loka-cartridge-v2, path .cartridge.format, data {}; CONTENT_HASH_MISMATCH: content_hash differs from the hash of cartridge (05 §11, CAR-05), path .content_hash, data {declared, computed}; ARTIFACT_DEFINITION_KEY_MISMATCH: a definition map key's cartridge_id or cartridge_version differs from the manifest's id or version, or its key from the definition's key (a policy has no key field, so only the first two apply; a kind other than its map's fails the propertyNames pattern, SCHEMA_VIOLATION); the schema cannot express this check; path the map member (.cartridge.facts["..."]), one diagnostic per differing field, data {field, declared, expected} with field cartridge_id, cartridge_version or key; LOCK_MANIFEST_MISMATCH: lock.capabilities differs from manifest.requires.capabilities for a key, which in R4 must be equal (path .cartridge.lock.capabilities.<key> even when the lock lacks it, data {capability, required, locked}, the absent side omitted); a registry-dependency closure will change this rule under a new format tag; CAPABILITY_NOT_INSTALLED: the lock names a key@version the installed kernel lacks (05 §6), path .cartridge.lock.capabilities.<key>, data {capability: key@version}; KERNEL_API_UNSUPPORTED: the installed kernel_api is outside the manifest's range (05 §3), path .cartridge.manifest.requires.kernel_api, data {installed}; CLIENT_FEATURE_UNSUPPORTED: the installed app lacks a required client feature (CAR-07), path .cartridge.manifest.requires.client_features[i], data {feature}. In the loader, suggested_capabilities is empty except for UNDECLARED_CAPABILITY. The loader checks an artifact in this order and stops at the first stage that fails, before any save mutation (CAR-07), reporting the first of that stage's diagnostics in list order (Diagnostic): ArtifactSize (ARTIFACT_TOO_LARGE); canonical decode (INVALID_JSON); cartridge.format (UNKNOWN_FORMAT); CartridgeArtifact (UNKNOWN_FIELD, SCHEMA_VIOLATION); content_hash (CONTENT_HASH_MISMATCH); definition keys (ARTIFACT_DEFINITION_KEY_MISMATCH); lock against requirements (LOCK_MANIFEST_MISMATCH; UNKNOWN_COMMAND and UNDECLARED_CAPABILITY re-run against the lock: every command an action uses has an owning capability, and every command and policy op a definition uses has its owning capability's key in the lock, CAR-07; and every room's owning capability too; events join when a frozen kind references one); references (UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE, v2 only: exits, entry and text keys); the installed kernel and app (CAPABILITY_NOT_INSTALLED, KERNEL_API_UNSUPPORTED, PINNED_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED, CLIENT_FEATURE_UNSUPPORTED). The loader re-checks the content_schema and rule_ir pins: the artifact crosses a trust boundary.

Diagnostic.description: A structured diagnostic (08 §6; 05 §8: every compile stage emits them). message_key is diagnostics. followed by the code in lowercase; data carries the code's facts as strings and integers; suggested_capabilities lists capability pins that would fix it (the key@version form requires uses), possibly none. A list of diagnostics is in one deterministic order (05 §8, CAR-04): by path, then code, comparing UTF-8 bytes, then by the canonical encoding of the whole diagnostic; an identical diagnostic appears once.

path.description: Where a diagnostic applies (08 §6). A compiler path is a source followed by steps; a loader path is steps only, relative to the artifact file, and empty for the whole file, so it is empty or starts with . or [. The source is the file's path relative to the cartridge root, / separated, without its .json extension (quests/missing_child, cartridge for cartridge.json); if a segment is not [a-z0-9_]+ or the file does not end in .json, the source is instead the whole relative path as a canonical JSON string literal (loka-numeric-v1). Steps: .name for an object member whose name is [a-z0-9_]+; ["..."] with the name as a canonical JSON string literal for any other member; [n] for array index n (decimal, no leading zeros). Example: quests/missing_child.objectives[2].target; a diagnostic about a whole file is its source alone.
